HEEWON STYLE — a KOREAN WEBTOON movie still PAINTED like a premium digital painting, the look of a dramatic manhwa cover. A 2:1 movie frame composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop (nothing important at the top or bottom edge). The shot the scene names (wide establishing, two-shot, close-up, over-the-shoulder) from a dramatic camera angle (low three-quarter, worm's-eye, high overhead or dutch), never a flat straight-on catalogue pose. Named characters' FACES are drawn exactly like the attached character sheet: the same clean confident ink linework and manhwa face design (eye shape, brows, nose, jaw, hairline and hair), recognisably those characters, in the clothes the scene gives them. EVERYTHING ELSE IS PAINTED: visible textured brushwork — loose digital-paint strokes and dry-brush, charcoal-like hatching that follow every fold of the silk and every plate of armour, the shadows built from layered strokes, the brightest ridges laid in with single confident strokes, a faint paper-and-canvas grain; at the edges of the garments the linework breaks into loose sketchy strokes. NOT flat cel-shading, NOT smooth airbrushed gradients, NOT a clean vector look, NOT photoreal, NOT 3D. Medium close two-shot at the bottom of the stone palace steps in Sabi at dusk. Prince Pung, a small boy of eight in a red robe with gold-striped black sleeves, sits on the lowest step holding up a thin strip of pale wood covered in neat brush characters with both hands, earnest and proud. Teenage Gyebek stands below him in chalk-grey white, sand on his shoulders, bent at the waist, staring at the marks he cannot read, his face very still. The strip of wood is the bright centre of the frame between their faces. One low sunset shaft from the left lights the wood and the boy's face; steps and silk crowds fall into umber shadow behind. CHARACTER SHEET, left to right: LEFT face = pung, SECOND face = gyebek. Copy each face exactly; give each person the dress the scene names. PRINCE PUNG — Look: Prince years: smooth beardless face, soft eyes, black hair in a topknot bound with a red-and-gold cord and a gold pin. Dress: Red robe with black sleeves striped in gold, gold-brocade crossed collar, braided red-and-gold cord sash. Colour #e6c76a. GYEBEK — Now: Boyhood (ch_gyebek_boy): a thin nameless river boy of about thirteen, barefoot, in a plain undyed WHITE hemp shirt and trousers with a rope belt; short-to-medium loose black hair, no topknot, no cap, no headband, no scarf, no armor; flat, watchful, unblinking eyes. Colour #d9b13a. PLACE Sabi (사비 (부여)) — attached board /pl_sabi_palace.png; keep this exact architecture and ground. Sabi palace on the Baengma river bluffs; Baekje giwa halls and pavilions. BACKGROUND AND LIGHT (painterly tenebrism): the background IS the place and the moment of the scene — open sky if they are in the sky, the hall if they are in a hall, the gate, the river, the snow — painted loosely in atmospheric brushwork (drifting smoke, cloud, haze, mist, falling snow, embers) in the scene's own colours, soft and out of focus, with a faint bokeh of small lights; it has colour, weather and depth — never a flat black void, never a detailed set; crowds and armies only as massed painted shapes dissolving into haze. ONE hard directional key light that belongs to the place (a brazier, a lamp, the sun through cloud, a torch, moonlight) rakes across the faces and clothes from the side or from below, modelling them in high contrast with deep painted shadows and a thin edge of the same light along the silhouette. Each character's colour lives in that light and in the atmosphere around them — never a glow aura or halo. Faces and bodies act the beat: real expressions, real weight, mid-motion. Faces from the sheet; new poses, never the sheet's stance. Each named person appears once, never cloned. Everyone wears period clothing of their own court (Korean, Tang, Yamato, Mohe furs), never European dress. No text, no speech bubbles, no panel borders, no watermark.
